messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For French, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Tant' | Intensifier marking a high degree of bitterness | French **si** (adv) + **amère** (fem. adj) → *si amère* ← back‑translation: “so bitter” | | è (1) | Copular verb linking implicit subject “it” to predicate | French **est** (3sg present of *être*) ← back‑translation: “is” | | amara | Predicate adjective denoting bitterness | French **amère** (fem. adj, agrees with implicit neuter) ← back‑translation: “bitter” | | che | Comparative subordinator introducing the clause | French **que** (conj.) ← back‑translation: “that” | | poco | Adverb indicating a small amount | French **un peu** (adv) ← back‑translation: “little” | | è (2) | Copular verb in the comparative clause (subject = death) | French **est** (3sg present of *être*) ← back‑translation: “is” | | più | Comparative adverb expressing “more” (direction: death > X) | French **plus** (comparative adv) – must appear in *la mort est **un peu plus** amère que X* ← back‑translation: “more” | | morte | Noun denoting the upper reference point of bitterness | French **mort** (fem. noun) ← back‑translation: “death” | | ma | Coordinating conjunction signalling contrast | French **mais** (conj.) ← back‑translation: “but” | | per | Preposition marking purpose | French **pour** (prep.) ← back‑translation: “in order to” | | trattar | Infinitive “to treat / discuss” | French **traiter** (inf.) ← back‑translation: “treat” | | del | Contraction of *di + il* → “of the” | French **du** (de + le) ← back‑translation: “of the” | | ben | Abstract noun “good” | French **bien** (n.) ← back‑translation: “good” | | ch'i' | Relative pronoun + personal pronoun “that I” | French **que j’** (rel. pron. + 1st‑sg pron.) ← back‑translation: “that I” | | vi | Locative adverb “there” | French **là** (adv.) ← back‑translation: “there” | | trovai | Simple past “found” (historic) | French **je trouvai** (passé simple) ← back‑translation: “found” | | dirò | Future “I will tell” | French **je dirai** (fut. simple) ← back‑translation: “I will tell” | | de | Preposition “of” | French **de** (prep.) ← back‑translation: “of” | | l'altre | Determiner + adjective “the other” | French **les autres** (det. + adj.) ← back‑translation: “the other” | | cose | Plural noun “things” | French **choses** (fem. pl.) ← back‑translation: “things” | | ch'i' (2) | Relative pronoun + personal pronoun “that I” | French **que j’** (rel. pron. + 1st‑sg pron.) ← back‑translation: “that I” | | v'ho | Auxiliary *avere* + locative clitic “there” → perfect | French **les ai** (aux. *avoir* + direct object pronoun) with implicit **là** understood → *je les ai (vu) là* ← back‑translation: “have … there” | | scorte | Past participle “seen” (agreeing fem. pl.) | French **vues** (fem. pl. past participle) ← back‑translation: “seen” |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable French components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: c’est si amère que la mort est un peu plus amère / c’est tellement amère que la mort n’est que légèrement plus amère / c’est si amère que la mort n’est qu’un peu plus amère - Line 8: pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là / afin de traiter du bien que j’ai découvert là / dans le but de traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé ici - Line 9: je dirai des autres choses que j’ai vues là / je raconterai des autres choses que j’ai observées là / je parlerai des autres choses que j’ai découvertes là

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into French lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line.

- **Line #: 7** - Target Text (from Step 4): c’est si amère que la mort est un peu plus amère; - Back‑Translation (literal): “it is so bitter that death is a little more bitter.” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): “So bitter is it that death is little more.” - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **OK**, Hallucination **OK**
- **Line #: 8** - Target Text (from Step 4): mais pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là, - Back‑Translation (literal): “but in order to treat the good that I found there,” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): “But in order to treat of the good that there I found,” - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- **Line #: 9** - Target Text (from Step 4): je dirai des autres choses que j’ai vues là. - Back‑Translation (literal): “I will say of the other things that I have seen there.” - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): “I will tell of the other things that I have seen there.” - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **FAIL** - Corrected Target Text: je dirai **les** autres choses que j’ai vues là.
**Overall Verification:** **UNVERIFIED** – failing line(s): 9
```text c’est si amère que la mort est un peu plus amère; mais pour traiter du bien que j’ai trouvé là, je dirai les autres choses que j’ai vues là. ```
